title: Copilot Studio: share autonomous agents with end users (run-only)
summary: Hold: the briefing says connector blocking has no documented automation, but Microsoft documents a PowerShell command that assigns connectors to the Blocked group. The setup-link instructions also omit the Copy sharing link menu needed to reach Copy link to set up. The roadmap dates, licensing prerequisites and listed control paths otherwise have supporting documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says autonomous agents previously could only be used and managed by makers.
claims.quote: Previously, autonomous agents could only be used and managed by makers, limiting their reach to the people who needed them.

claims.quote: Run-only sharing enables makers to securely share autonomous agents with end users, allowing users to benefit from agent-driven automation without requiring edit permissions or ownership.

claims.claim: Makers can share a published autonomous agent that has triggers.
claims.quote: You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Recipients do not receive a notification when the agent is shared.
claims.quote: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them. Makers must copy and send the can use link to end users.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The recipient must activate the agent and connect every trigger, tool and workflow that requires their credentials before it can run.
claims.quote: An autonomous agent can't run until you connect every trigger, tool, and workflow that requires your credentials.

claims.claim: Recipients can change only the trigger options the maker permits.
claims.quote: Users complete the required connections on the shared-agent page, and can change only the trigger options you allow.

claims.claim: The maker chooses editable trigger options with Editable by user.
claims.quote: If you're sharing this agent with others to use, choose which options users can or can't configure themselves by turning on or off Editable by user for each option.

claims.claim: Recipients cannot change the agent's instructions, tools or other authoring settings.
claims.quote: You can't change the agent's instructions, tools, or other authoring settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Recipients cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.
claims.quote: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.

claims.claim: A workflow used as a tool in a shared autonomous agent can accept only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.claim: Before run-only sharing, triggers and tools must be configured for user authentication.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.claim: This autonomous-agent experience uses the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Use triggers to create autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Editing rights are separate and assigned through environment security roles.
claims.quote: Add users to the agent's environment, and then assign users editing rights through the environment's security roles.

claims.claim: The recipient's connections determine the account permissions available to the agent.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.claim: The maker's instructions and tools determine the agent's response to event data.
claims.quote: The trigger sends event details to the agent. Your agent's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with those details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Data policies govern Copilot Studio connector use in the environments covered by the policy.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not explain the handling of an already-running shared autonomous instance when a trigger is blocked or a data policy changes.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared autonomous agents data policy running. Opened Configure data policies for agents; read Troubleshoot data policy enforcement excerpts. General real-time enforcement is documented, but not treatment of a shared autonomous run already in progress.

claims.claim: An agent running under end-user credentials cannot perform an action the end user lacks permission to perform.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Maker updates prompt users to accept changes and can require new or updated connections on the management page.
claims.quote: Republish the agent after you change a trigger, its instructions, or its tools. Updating an agent prompts users to accept the new changes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Autonomous runs can start from events without a user opening a chat.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: Learn documents no approval setting specific to run-only shared autonomous agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous shared agents approval human approval setting; shared autonomous agent approval. Opened sharing, setup, triggers and workflow-tool pages; read multistage approval excerpts. Workflow design approvals exist, but no run-only-specific approval setting was found.

claims.claim: End users need to bookmark the management URL for health checks, repairs and consent to maker updates.
claims.quote: End users need to bookmark the agent management URL to check their agent's health, fix the agent, consent to maker updates to the agent, and other management tasks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup article does not state what administrators can see of individual recipients' instances.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous shared agents admin instances; shared autonomous agent disabled maker administrator. Opened Set up a shared autonomous agent and Share agents with other users and makers. Neither describes administrator visibility into individual activated instances.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing and setup pages do not explain what happens to recipient instances when the maker leaves or is disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous agent disabled maker administrator. Opened Share agents with other users and makers and Set up a shared autonomous agent. They describe sharing, updates and connections, not the lifecycle of activated instances after disabling the maker.

Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.

claims.claim: The data-policy route runs through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors > Microsoft Copilot Studio > Block.
claims.quote: Select Security, and then select Data and privacy. ... Select Data policy. ... select New Policy ... Add an environment ... select the environment in the Available tab ... Add to policy. ... Assign connectors ... select Block.

claims.claim: Configuring the data policy requires tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents makers from adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents ... configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: An enforced event-trigger restriction produces a detailed error in the Triggers section.
claims.quote: If the policy is enforced, a detailed error message appears in the Triggers section on the Overview page. The message mentions the name of the data policy and suggests you contact your admin.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy creates a policy, and its own reference does not describe assigning a specified connector to Blocked.
claims.quote:
Creates a new DLP policy in the tenant by using the NewPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object.
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and data-policy paragraph
claims.claim: Automation for assigning the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector to Blocked is not documented.
claims.quote:
Adds the given connectors to the given group of the DLP policy.
-Classification: ... Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api null with powershell call 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <PolicyGuid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <ConnectorObjects>' and this source URL. State in the note that ConnectorObjects identifies the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector, with each object containing id, type and name as required by the reference. Replace the prose's inference from New-DlpPolicy with 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy assigns the selected connector objects to the Blocked group.' Add the reference URL to sources and mirror the correction in the rendered table.

claims.claim: For an ungrouped environment, maker credential controls are at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: Select Manage. ... Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings ... Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Copilot Studio agents ... Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.claim: Grouped environments must use Manage > Environment groups > group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options instead of the individual environment page.
claims.quote:
You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.
Select Environments or Environment groups.

claims.claim: Configuring the maker credential setting for an environment group requires a tenant admin with access to that group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: Learn warns that blocking maker-provided credentials makes scheduled or autonomously triggered agents fail due to missing credentials.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: The maker credential setting immediately changes the authentication requirements for all agents in the affected environment.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: No documented automation for Control maker credential options was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Control maker credential options API PowerShell pac admin; Control maker credential options Power Platform API; Copilot Studio maker credentials organization table. Opened Control maker-provided credentials for authentication; read pac admin excerpts. No setting-specific operation found.

claims.claim: Embedded-maker-credential sharing controls are at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure.
Select Settings, and then select Features.
Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: Connections configured for end-user credentials are not subject to the embedded-maker-credential connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.claim: No documented automation for Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials API PowerShell setting; embedded maker credentials Set-. Opened Configure sharing agents with embedded maker credentials; read Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials and Manage feature settings excerpts. No automation found.

claims.claim: No documented API for granting the shared-autonomous-agent Can use permission was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared autonomous agent Can use Dataverse Web API sharing permissions; Can use autonomous API sharing; autonomous Can use GrantAccess. claims.claim: Recipients can pause and resume triggers using the Enabled toggle on the management page.
claims.quote: To pause a trigger without removing its configuration, turn the Enabled toggle off. Turn it on again when you want the trigger to run.

claims.claim: The management page's Activity tab lets recipients review recent and failed runs.
claims.quote: Use the Activity tab to review recent runs and identify failed runs.
